title: Be going to
subtitle: Plans, and things you can see coming
review: Written by Claude in the format of the French tense pages. Check the examples and the level.
intro: Use it for a **plan you already have**, and for something you can **see is about to happen**. The future starts from something that is true **now**: your decision, or what you can see.

examples.fr: I **am going to visit** my uncle tomorrow.
She **is going to study** medicine.
We **are going to buy** a new house next year.
They **are going to play** football after school.
I **am going to be** a teacher.
Look at those clouds. It **is going to rain**.
examples.en: I can see the clouds now.

examples.fr: Be careful! You **are going to fall**.
The bus is very full. We **are going to be** late.
She is running very fast. She **is going to win**.
Hurry up! The film **is going to start**.
Sit down. I **am going to tell** you a story.
Watch this. I **am going to jump**.
The baby **is going to cry**.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.note: The verb after *going to* never changes: *she is going to play*, not *she is going to plays*.

blocks.title: Speaking
points: People often say the short forms: **I'm going to**, **she's going to**, **they're going to**.
In fast speech *going to* sounds like **gonna**. You will hear it in songs and films. Do not write it at school.
With the verb **go**, people often just say *I'm going to the market tomorrow* (not *going to go*). Both are correct.

blocks.text: tomorrow, tonight, next week / month / year, this weekend, soon, later, in two days, after school, when I grow up, Look!, Be careful! …

blocks.formula: am / is / are + **not** + going to + verb

examples.fr: I **am not going to tell** you.
He **isn't going to come**.
We **aren't going to wait**.
It **isn't going to rain** today.

blocks.formula: **Am / Is / Are** + subject + going to + verb ?

examples.fr: **Are** you **going to help** me?
examples.en: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

examples.fr: **Is** she **going to come** to the party?
What **are** you **going to do** tomorrow?
Where **are** they **going to live**?
When **is** he **going to call**?
**Going to**: you decided before. *I am going to buy a bike. I have the money.*
**Will**: you decide now, while speaking. *The phone is ringing. I will answer it.*
**Going to**: you can see it. *Look at the sky. It is going to rain.*
**Will**: you think so. *I think it will rain tomorrow.*
